summary: Verified the SEC-001/SEC-002 security fixes on the PUBLIC preview URL (https://arpita-analytics.preview.emergentagent.com) plus a frontend regression smoke test. Created /app/backend/tests/test_security_fixes.py (12 pytest cases, all passing): POST/GET/PUT/DELETE/PATCH /api/status return 404 on the public URL (no data leak, no 'client_name' in body); GET /api/ and GET /api return 200 with exactly {"status":"ok"}; CORS on the public URL never emits Access-Control-Allow-Credentials (neither on a simple GET with an Origin header nor on an OPTIONS preflight) — SEC-002 wildcard+credentials combo is resolved. App-layer CORS verified directly against uvicorn: OPTIONS preflight for POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH is rejected with 400 'Disallowed CORS method' and access-control-allow-methods is exactly 'GET'. Backend supervisor logs show a clean reload, no tracebacks/errors. Frontend smoke (1920x1080): page loads, hero ARPITA/NAIR present, /assets/arpita-portrait-2026.jpg loads (911x824 natural size), 0 broken images, 9 nav links, nav click scrolls (scrollY=2663), ZERO network requests to /api/* (confirming the site is unaffected by the backend change), 0 console errors and 0 page errors.

minor.issue: The preview edge/ingress rewrites CORS headers: public responses carry 'access-control-allow-methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, HEAD, PATCH' and 'access-control-allow-origin: *' regardless of the app's allow_methods=['GET'], and a POST preflight returns 204 instead of the app's 400. This is platform infra, not app code, and is not exploitable here (no write routes exist and allow-credentials is absent everywhere). Flagged only so the app-level allow_methods=['GET'] is not assumed to be observable from the public URL.

lib.db (Mongo client/db) is still imported and a connection is opened/closed in lifespan even though no route uses the DB. Dead dependency — consider removing or keeping intentionally for future routes.

critical_code_review_comments: allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False is now safe, but for a static portfolio that makes zero API calls the CORS middleware could be dropped entirely (or origins pinned to the site host) to shrink the surface further.
Unused MongoDB import/connection in server.py (lib.db) — remove if no DB-backed routes are planned.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (smoke: load, hero, portrait, nav, no console errors, 0 API calls)

seed_data_creation: None — no writable endpoints remain; no data created.
test_credentials: None required (no auth on this app)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Public URL https://arpita-analytics.preview.emergentagent.com (env var preview_endpoint). Backend has exactly one route: GET /api/ -> {'status':'ok'}; /api/status is gone (404). Security regression suite: /app/backend/tests/test_security_fixes.py — run with `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_security_fixes.py -v`. IMPORTANT: the preview edge injects permissive Access-Control-Allow-Methods/Origin headers, so CORS method restrictions must be asserted against http://localhost:8001 (see TestCORSAppLayer); Access-Control-Allow-Credentials can and should be asserted absent on both layers. Frontend makes zero /api calls — do not expect any network integration. Full frontend suite results are in iteration_1.json (all passing) and were intentionally not re-run.
rca_of_the_issue: No defects in the fix. Two initially failing CORS assertions were harness/infra artifacts, not app bugs: the preview edge proxy overwrites CORS response headers (returning 204 + all methods for a POST preflight), masking the app's own allow_methods=['GET'] and 400 rejection. Re-asserted at the uvicorn layer, confirming the intended behavior; the security-relevant header (Access-Control-Allow-Credentials) is absent at both layers.
